desk.headline: Adjusted HEPS up 17.1% to 160.6c on revenue up 4.2% to R27.4bn; dividend up 17.6% to 100c; qualitative outlook only

numbers.heps_basis: adjusted HEPS (company measure); IFRS HEPS not stated in the results release

other.label: Profit after tax and exceptional items

results: Revenue rose 4.2% to R27.4bn and normalised EBITDA rose 5.4% to R5.18bn, lifting the margin to 18.9% from 18.6%.
Adjusted HEPS jumped 17.1% to 160.6c, well ahead of revenue growth, helped by efficiency gains, digital savings and fewer shares after buybacks.
Hospital and emergency revenue grew 4.4% to R26.8bn and paid patient days rose 1.7%; primary care revenue fell 6.9% after losing a large occupational health contract.
Netcare says digital projects have saved R881m since FY2022, more than the R670m it has invested.
Final dividend of 56.0c takes the year to 100.0c (up 17.6%); with R1.04bn of buybacks, R2.2bn went back to shareholders. Net debt rose slightly to 1.2x EBITDA.

guidance.summary: Netcare gives no numerical FY2027 targets. It sees early signs of a better economy, but says job and affordability pressure is holding back growth in medical scheme members; it plans to balance price and volume, keep cutting costs and use its capacity better.

points: CEO Richard Friedland said medical schemes are raising premiums well above inflation, cutting benefits and pushing members into low-cost networks, which weighs on revenue.
He said finding efficiencies took hard work, but gave operating leverage despite modest revenue growth; seven AI prediction models are in development.
Incoming CEO Melanie da Costa flagged unreliable municipal water, worsened by an expected El Nino, as a significant risk for the year ahead.
Netcare is adding groundwater treatment plants (five running, two being built, six more planned) to rely less on municipal supply.
Friedland steps down at the end of December 2026; da Costa takes over on 1 January 2027.
call.source: EWN (23 Nov 2026) and TimesLIVE / Business Day interview with the incoming CEO (24 Nov 2026)

watch: Medical scheme membership and network restrictions, which management says are capping hospital demand.
Water supply disruptions at Gauteng hospitals during an El Nino year.
The CEO handover on 1 January 2027 and whether margin gains from digital savings continue.
